title: Creation of Cardiac Tissue Exhibiting Mechanical Integration of Spheroids Using 3D Bioprinting
protocol: Generate and culture human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) on 6-well plates coated with basement membrane matrix.
Differentiate hiPSCs into hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs).
Isolate the cardiomyocytes using Trypsin/EDTA 0.05% for 5 min at room temperature.
Neutralize Trypsin with Trypsin inhibitor 0.0125%.
Pool isolated cardiomyocytes and transfer into one 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge cell suspension for 5 min at 250 x g at room temperature to obtain a pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in RPMI/B-27 cell media.
Pipette 20 µL of cells in cell media and stain with an equal amount of Trypan Blue solution.
Count and obtain the concentration and cell viability using an automated cell counter or manual hemocytometer.
Initiate the human cardiac fibroblast (HCF) (adult ventricular type) cell line.
Passage and isolate HCFs according to culturing protocols.
Pipette 20 µL of cells in cell media and stain with an equal amount of Trypan Blue solution.
Use an automated cell counter or a manual hemocytometer to count and obtain the concentration and cell viability of the new cell suspension.
Initiate the human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) line as described.
Pipette 20 µL of cells in cell media.
Stain with an equal amount of 0.4% Trypan Blue solution.

Mix the three cell types (hiPSC-CM, HCFs, and HUVECs) in RPMI/B-27 cell media to generate a stock of mixed cell solution at a hiPSC-CM:HCF:HUVEC ratio of 70:15:15 and concentration of 165,000 cells per mL.
Distribute the mixed cell solution into ultra-low attachment 96-well U-bottom plates at 200 µL per well.
Incubate the 96-well plates for 3 days (37°C, 5% carbon dioxide, 95% humidity).
Inspect for the presence of mixed cell multicellular spheroids at the center and bottom of individual wells under light microscopy.
Load the plates containing the spheroids into the magazines of the scaffold-free spheroid-based 3D bioprinter.
Turn on the 3D bioprinter and execute the 3D bioprinting software.
Click "Auxillary", "Operation Preparation", "Inspect Mode", and then "Home Return".
Click the green icon under "Start" to begin spheroid inspection.
Watch for the spheroid diameters to appear under the column "(2) Dia (µm)" on the screen.
To estimate the average spheroid diameter to the nearest 100 µm, click "Initial settings".
Enter the average spheroid diameter into Stack Z pitch (µm).
Click "Total", the number under "Layers" should readjust automatically.
Click "Apply" to confirm the settings.
Click "Needle Array Map".
Go to "Layer No." and select the desired layer for 3D bioprinting.
Draw the desired 3D bioprinting design on the map by selecting individual spheroid positions.
Click "Apply" to confirm the 3D bioprinting design.
Click "Needle Array Check".
Input values into "OffsetZ (µm)", ranging from 0 to 500 µm, starting with 500 µm and decreasing by 100 µm to adjust camera focus.
Set "Diameter (µm)" in the inspection parameters to the desired range.
Set "Roundness (%)" to the desired percentage.
Set "Smoothness (%)" to the desired percentage.
Click "Apply" to confirm the settings.
Click "Presence".
Update the "Diameter (µm)" to the same settings as in the previous step.
Click "Apply" to confirm the settings.
Click "Stack Mode".
Start spheroid pick up using the nozzle of the 3D bioprinter by vacuum suction.
Place spheroids in specific locations in a needle array.
Incubate the 3D bioprinted patch with the needle array for 3 days at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity.
Gently slide the plastic cover upwards to remove the 3D bioprinted patch from the needle array after incubation.
Lubricate the needles with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) if necessary for easier removal of the patch.
Pick up the plastic cover with the 3D bioprinted patch using sterile forceps and transfer it into a 35 mm dish containing RPMI/B-27 cell media.
Gently shake the plastic cover in the RPMI/B-27 cell media to release the patch into the media.
Inspect the 3D bioprinted patch under light microscopy to ensure functionality.
Incubate the released 3D bioprinted patch in the 35 mm dish for 3 days or longer at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity.
